## Riparian areas
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Important ecological areas
    - Nesting habitat
    - Transportation cooridors
    - Refuge for benficial plants  and insects
    
![](figs/eggs.jpg){width=48%}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

- Hydrologically important
  - Bank stabilization
  - Water temperature regulation
  - Reduce flooding risk
  


![](figs/corridor.png)   

:::

## Riparian areas
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Part of the farm
    - Account for 5 to 10% of the farm area
    - Important source of forage
    
![[Cows and Fish Program](https://cowsandfish.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/greenzone3rd.pdf)](figs/riparian grazing.png){width=45%}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Riparian areas are maintained to intercept and store nutrients
    - BMP to improve water quality

![[Stewart et al. 2010](https://publications.gc.ca/site/eng/387724/publication.html)](figs/Buffer_man.png){width=40%}   
:::
    
## Riparian areas as filters
### Typical prairie riparian area during the snowmelt period
- Most P loading occurs during the spring snowmelt
- Frozen soils and dead and dormant vegetation
    - Filtering capacity is not not very good during the most critical period
- Vegetation can be a source of P
    
::: {layout-ncol=2}

![](figs/frozen2.jpg)

![Lobb](figs/frozen1.jpg)

:::

## Research objectives


::: {.column width="70%"}

### Can we use riparian cattle grazing to reduce the risk of P loss?

1. Assess the distribution of P in two directions

**Vertical**

- Biomass, Litter, Organic layer, Ah (0-10)

**Longitudinal**

- Upper, mid, lower 

2. Quantify the net change in P following grazing
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](figs/bio_litter.jpg)
:::
## Location

### Four riparian areas at the [MBFI](https://www.mbfi.ca/) research farm
- South-western Manitoba

![[Koiter & Malone 2025](http://doi.org/10.1002/jeq2.70012)](figs/Figure 1.png)

## Treatments
::: {.column width="50%"}

1.  Control
2.  Grazing
3.  High-density grazing
4.  Mowing

- Fall grazing
    - Drier soils
    - Protect habitat
    - Extending gazing season
    - Remove P prior to winter
    
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](figs/grazing1.jpg)
:::

## Sampling
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Sample collection 
- Pre- and post-grazing
- Biomass and litter
    - 0.25 m^2^ quadrate
- Organic and Ah
    - Soil probe
    
### Sample analysis
- Wieghed
- Dried and homogenized
- Water extraction
- Molybdate–ascorbic acid method

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

![](figs/sampling1.jpg){width=75%}

![](figs/sampling2.jpg){width=75%}
:::
## Distribution of P

- Biomass and litter are large sources of P

![[Koiter & Malone 2025](http://doi.org/10.1002/jeq2.70012)](figs/Figure 2.png)

## Biomass

- High density grazing and mowing reduced the amount of P
- More P removed in lower slope locations

![[Koiter & Malone 2025](http://doi.org/10.1002/jeq2.70012)](figs/Figure 3.png)

## Litter
- No treatment effect
- High variability 

![[Koiter & Malone 2025](http://doi.org/10.1002/jeq2.70012)](figs/Figure 4.png)

## Organic layer
- No treatment effect
- High variability 

![[Koiter & Malone 2025](http://doi.org/10.1002/jeq2.70012)](figs/Figure 5.png)

## Ah

- No treatment effect
- High variability 

![[Koiter & Malone 2025](http://doi.org/10.1002/jeq2.70012)](figs/Figure 6.png)

## Variabilty

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Variabilty is high
  - Above and below ground
  - Even in the control plots
  - Makes detecting small changes difficult

![](figs/species.jpg) 
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

- Hotspots
  - Manure/urine
  - Plant species
  - Biophysical processes 

![](figs/manure.jpg)  
:::  
  
## Conclusions

- Fall riparian grazing reduced the amount of biomass P
    - Reduced risk of P loss during snowmelt

- Variability is high
  - Sampling design needs to accomdate this

![](figs/cow_crop2.jpg){fig-align="center"}
